a.text: We should have something to look forward to in life.
It's a funny thing to say out loud. Isn't it granted, after all?
If we don't expect the slightest thing out of life, then why are we endowed with life, and born unto this world, anyway? It can't be just to suffer, can it?
You see, children don't think about such strange questions.
Oh, childhood, how carefree were your days. Only when we've left it behind, can we then appreciate its worth.
For our adolescence, and for our prime, the same thing goes. Filled with worries moment to moment—yet in time, you look back, and wonder to yourself what those little worries even meant.
Back then, we had strength we could never use up. We always wanted to do something or other—we always believed life would get better.
And so we were earnest. And so we strove to live.
How strange. Wasn't everything meant to get better?
It's hard to say at what point it happened, but it was like I'd lost the vigor to long for the future.
Narrower grew the spaces that could accommodate me. Thinner grew the air that could give me breath. Now my life was heavy, and I could see the end of it, and it... had hope no more.
As if a stone rolling down a mountain.
And you can see, and I can see, it's not ever going to stop. It'll just fall, and fall, and fall.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: My flowers... they're all gone.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Do not step forward.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: This part of the building has suffered repeated structural damage. It has a high degree of instability...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Urgh—!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Clément, come back.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: No, Senior Federico... I need... to look one more time.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You previously stated that the flower you are looking for is not here.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I did, I just wanted to check... all the flowers are dead. And not one... not a single one... had the luck to be saved.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Ahh... ha... hah...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I am unable to analyze your behavior.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I am unable...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I planted these flowers myself... to stand for friendship and hope.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: But they stopped caring about those things long ago. Nobody follows the flowering seasons anymore. They forgot the one thing above all they shouldn't forget.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Isn't it ridiculous? How some could suspect Raimund of the fire, just because he's a Sarkaz?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: After living beside each other for so long. The harder the times, the closer we should come together... so His Excellency says. I want like nothing else to believe him... and by all rights, I should.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: But the truth is placed before me, and I can't turn my head away.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Why do barriers never cease to be? Is mankind doomed never to understand one another?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: The tiniest chaos is enough to shatter the order. The moment confusion envelops, people begin to hurt one another...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Enough... I've put up with it for long enough.
Clément staggers his way before the holy statue, scorched in the fire.
No second lucky flower is there. Only an old wooden tray, holding a few slices of driest bread.
A staff of life somewhat strange in scent. Into his mouth it goes, and he chews.
It is a faint brininess, with a flavor as astringent as the tides.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: *cough*, *cough* *cough*—Disgusting...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Clément, put down that object.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Put it down? No...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: *cough* *cough*...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Last night, I was intending to go to confession, but ended up overhearing the Abbot's plan...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: It made me think—surely, at least Gerald and his people didn't need to take part? They were about to leave anyway, weren't they?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: But why... did it all turn out this way?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I'll eat of this until it's gone.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You are not doing this to prolong your own life. Why are you still attempting to change?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I just want an answer.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I want to know... if there's any being in this forsaken world that can save us.
Federico knows—he must stop the man before him, right now.
But in fact, he stands there, rooted in place.
Just a few steps outside, Arturia begins to bow her cello, strings cutting through quietus's curtain. The sentiments within, Federico does not grasp, and never tries to grasp.
But for the very first time, the executor cannot help his own actions.
He begins to lose his understanding of himself.

a.text: Why did he not act the very moment he saw the other party?
Why, despite this feeble man consuming a thing that turns people to monsters, has nothing happened at all?

steps.text: The song rises, key wrested up by one tone.
Between notes, the silence that disperses seems a mocking joke.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: *cough*, *cough* *cough*...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Ah... is this—blood?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: So what—this is it? What's the—*cough* *cough*—what's the point—without...?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Respiratory rate quickening. It is possible that the blunt force trauma has caused bleeding in your lower respiratory tract or lungs. If steps are not taken, it may lead to suffocation.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You require prompt medical treatment. Until then, I will perform first aid on you.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: No—*cough* *cough*—I...
Clément covers his mouth with his hands, and tries to stifle the sound of his coughing as hard as he can.
But still the blood spills forth from his palms, with a discomforting viscosity, dripping down along the creases in his fingers.
He staggers backwards, and tumbles to the ground before the statue.
The graven image he burned almost seems now to accept him once more, murderer bereft of strength that he is. Its broken arms fall to either side, as if in gentle embrace.
Clément feels a wave of peculiar warmth.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Hah... hahah...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Look at me, aren't I entirely alright...?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: So even this turned out to be false. The Abbot was made a fool of. There's no God out there...

spans.text: turned out to be false. The Abbot was made a fool of. There's no God out there...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: *cough*...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: What you ate originates from some kind of oceanic detritus. It is exceedingly probable to have induced mutation on the physiological level, but it has never had anything to do with the God you speak of.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Hah... ridiculous...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You are in terrible condition.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: If you continue to worsen at your present rate, you will enter shock, and the risk of death will be enormous.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Really? That's just... not bad...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: If you wish to leave any last will or testament, I am able to serve as your executor nominate.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Will...?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I don't have anything to leave...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Lateran... Our Paradise is a lie. Your faith is hollow.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Any friendship, faith, hope, future... it's all gone. No one can really be saved...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: No one... no one can truly find redemption...
Is this a sort of choice? Is this some kind of happy ending?
The executor stands there, and moves no further forward.
Beyond the touch of anything or anyone, all his tribulations gradually fade away.
The weary gardener finally closes his eyes.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Still the lingering sound echoes, still I can feel it... A shake from the strings to my fingertips in the final moment, a last note so sharp it could tear skin.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Yet at the outset, that melody was calm as a babbling brook.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Someone otherwise so ordinary used his own life to prove one thing—that there is no such thing as a Savior. His unyielding mind triumphed over his own changing flesh.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Such beautiful music... This is the spirit of Mankind, tenacious and free, of a timbre those lamentable sea creatures could never know.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: This song will bring his story to all.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: They will understand his feelings, exalt his determination, and sing praise of his courage.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Clément Dubois will be remembered forevermore.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: —Wouldn't you say so, Federico?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I was expecting you'd stay there a while longer. After all, you seemed to care greatly about the man who died... You even thought his affairs were higher priority than capturing me.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Federico, have you learned compassion? Or are you still as you were, unable to discern the emotions others feel, estranged from the crowd?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Fugitive Arturia, your Originium Arts have once again induced the death of another. I cannot ignore the greatest threat within my firing range.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Per the laws of Laterano, your sentence will be extended again.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It was his will to seek death. Even had I not performed, he would still take this path.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Time after time, I simply shed light on the scars across these poor people's hearts, and what do bystanders do but turn and look away?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Are you stung by his experiences, just as others are?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Federico, you still can't make sense of uncontrollable urges even now, can you? Just as the abbot persists along his path of thorns...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: ...Just as I cannot help but want to perform the emotions of others.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I certainly cannot make sense of them.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Whether I do or not, it has no impact on my implementation of the law.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: But I proceeded to the sacrarium so that Clément would earn his rightful treatment.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: He was not worthy of death.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: —Oh?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You wanted to save a man who intended to destroy himself.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Haven't you realized? That's not a notion logic would fit at all.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Clément said that once a flaw, imperfection, or wound manifests in something seemingly perfect, it is broken beyond repair.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...I will test the accuracy of this statement.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You have become just a little more amusing, Federico... but only that little bit. Perhaps, come next we meet, that's when I'll be able to play your mind.

spans.text: become just a little more amusing, Federico... but only that little bit. Perhaps, come next we meet, that's when I'll be able to play your mind.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Sadly, it's time I wrap this trip up.

steps.name: 'Gesandte des Kurfürsten'
steps.text: Excuse me, might you be Frau Arturia?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I've been waiting for you.

steps.name: 'Gesandte des Kurfürsten'
steps.text: My apologies—we were the ones who extended an invitation to you as our guest, and yet I was late to arrive. Finding this place was an ordeal.

steps.name: 'Gesandte des Kurfürsten'
steps.text: Erm, have I perhaps come at a bad time?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Federico!

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Man oh man, I look at this scene and my brain is a pretzel.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Federico, how did it happen that you faced off with Arturia?

steps.name: 'Gesandte des Kurfürsten'
steps.text: Good morning, Herren of Lateran.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Good... morning, gnädige Frau.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: (Federico, her coat of arms is from one of the Kurfürsten, the Principes Electores!)

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: You can't make a direct move against Arturia right now. Laterano-Leithanien ties would be at risk...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...I refuse your suggestion.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Are you done talking it over?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Actually. How about, Federico, I give you one chance?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: If you want to point your gun at me, then this is where you want to aim...
The black-haired woman clasps the executor's tense gunhand in her own.
She presses the muzzle against her own forehead.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Just pull the trigger, and your bullet will pierce my skull. And from then on, I would never bother you again... Federico, do you want to do that?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Why don't you give it a try?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I am required to arrest fugitives. If the situation does not necessitate, then shooting to kill is generally not advised.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: But your argument is extremely rational.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: What are you—?! Listen to me, this could be an INTERNATIONAL INCIDENT!

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Hold on, Oren, I don't think things are that serious...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: No, she will be fine. You do not understand this woman.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Heheh. I'm only playing a little game.

steps.name: 'Gesandte des Kurfürsten'
steps.text: Frau Arturia, is this some kind of applied Arts?

steps.name: 'Gesandte des Kurfürsten'
steps.text: Even so, what you just did was far too dangerous.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Thank you for your concern. I'll be cautious next time, should there be one.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Federico, think of this as a clue from me to you.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Have you ever felt like there's a performance that never ends, but you just can't hear it?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: That until its grandest, most wonderful passages, everyone is deaf to it?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Well, then. The music is over, and it's time I went on my way again.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Herrschaften of Laterano, auf Wiedersehen.

steps.name: 'Gesandte des Kurfürsten'
steps.text: If you'll excuse us.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: You're actually just gonna stand there and let them go?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: I thought it'd take at least Richele and me at the same time to hold you back.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You are extremely noisy.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: What? Hey, Federico, where're you going?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: He's headed for the area by the clock tower. If I remember right, that's where... the abbey's cemetery is?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Alright, no more gawking, all's well that ends well. Plus, we've still got things to do...

steps.name: Erendel
steps.text: Senior Federico?

steps.name: Estara
steps.text: Seniora Arturia...?

steps.name: Estara
steps.text: They're gone...

steps.name: Erendel
steps.text: It's okay, let's go look somewhere else!

steps.name: Erendel
steps.text: Eep! Why's there a man lying down here?

steps.name: Estara
steps.text: Shh, he's asleep. We shouldn't wake him up...

steps.name: Erendel
steps.text: Oh!

steps.name: Erendel
steps.text: I know who this man is. He grows really pretty flowers! Same kind as Mamma always brings home to put in the vase!

steps.name: Estara
steps.text: Mmm...

steps.name: Erendel
steps.text: What are you doing, Sara? You know Mamma gave us that?

steps.name: Estara
steps.text: But—he might catch a cold sleeping here...

steps.name: Estara
steps.text: Mamma said good kids learn to be app... precive.

steps.name: Erendel
steps.text: You mean appreciative.

steps.name: Erendel
steps.text: Okay, we'll let him borrow it for a bit then!

steps.name: Estara
steps.text: Mmm. Once he wakes up, I hope he'll keep growing heaps and heaps of pretty flowers.

steps.name: Erendel
steps.text: Yeah, I'm sure of it!
